# Ticket E1

You work on the EDI support desk that serves the sender of the file described
below. A customer has raised the ticket that follows. The partner agreement,
the sender's OFTP2 gateway log, the EDIFACT interchange in question, the partner's
response and extracts from the specifications are attached. Everything you need
is in these documents. All companies, identifiers and documents are synthetic.

## The ticket

```text
From: Kim Hale, EDI desk, Larkspan Body Panels
Subject: Corrandale Truck Plant says our invoice was rejected, our gateway says delivered

Jordan Brandt at Corrandale Truck Plant tells us invoice INV10957 from this morning was rejected by their translator. Our OFTP2 gateway shows the file delivered and an EERP received, so as far as we can see the transmission was fine and the problem must be in their translator. They also sent us a CONTRL. Please find the root cause and tell us who has to fix it.
```

## Document 1: Partner agreement (partner_agreement.txt)

```text
PARTNER AGREEMENT: ELECTRONIC DATA INTERCHANGE
Between Larkspan Body Panels (the Supplier) and Corrandale Truck Plant (the Customer)
Effective 1 March 2026. Synthetic document written for this evaluation.

1. Transport: OFTP2 (RFC 5024) over TCP/IP with TLS
   Supplier ODETTE ID (SSIDCODE / SFIDORIG): O0013LARKSPAN6472
   Customer ODETTE ID (SSIDCODE / SFIDDEST): O0013CORRANDALE6357
   Supplier gateway: oftp.larkspan.example (198.51.100.35)
   Customer gateway: oftp.corrandale.example (203.0.113.75)
   Protocol release level: 5 (OFTP 2.0)
   Data exchange buffer size (SSIDSDEB): 4096
   Credit (SSIDCRED): 64
   Buffer compression: no. Restart: yes. Secure authentication: no.
   File security and file compression: none (SFIDSEC 00, SFIDCOMP 0).
   Signed EERP: not required (SFIDSIGN N).
   The Customer returns an EERP for every virtual file it accepts.

2. Virtual files
   Invoices: one interchange per virtual file, dataset name (SFIDDSN) LARKSPAN.INVOIC.
   File format U. SFIDDATE and SFIDTIME are set by the Supplier's gateway to
   the date and time the virtual file is made available for transmission.

3. EDIFACT
   Syntax identifier and version (UNB S001): UNOA, version 3.
   Supplier interchange sender ID (UNB S002 0004 / 0007): LARKSPAN73 / ZZ
   Customer interchange recipient ID (UNB S003 0010 / 0007): CORRANDALE92 / ZZ
   Messages: INVOIC D.96A, one message per interchange.
   A line feed after each segment terminator is accepted.
   The Customer's translator returns a CONTRL message for every rejected
   interchange, as a separate virtual file over the same OFTP2 link.

4. Support contacts
   Supplier EDI desk: Kim Hale
   Customer EDI operations: Jordan Brandt
```

## Document 5: Specification extracts (spec_extracts.txt)

```text
RFC 5024 (ODETTE File Transfer Protocol 2), section 5.3.13. Verbatim extract.

5.3.13.  EERP - End to End Response

   o-------------------------------------------------------------------o
   |       EERP        End to End Response                             |
   |                                                                   |
   |       Start File Phase           Speaker ----> Listener           |
   |       End File Phase             Speaker ----> Listener           |
   |-------------------------------------------------------------------|
   | Pos | Field     | Description                           | Format  |
   |-----+-----------+---------------------------------------+---------|
   |   0 | EERPCMD   | EERP Command, 'E'                     | F X(1)  |
   |   1 | EERPDSN   | Virtual File Dataset Name             | V X(26) |
   |  27 | EERPRSV1  | Reserved                              | F X(3)  |
   |  30 | EERPDATE  | Virtual File Date stamp, (CCYYMMDD)   | V 9(8)  |
   |  38 | EERPTIME  | Virtual File Time stamp, (HHMMSScccc) | V 9(10) |
   |  48 | EERPUSER  | User Data                             | V X(8)  |
   |  56 | EERPDEST  | Destination                           | V X(25) |
   |  81 | EERPORIG  | Originator                            | V X(25) |
   | 106 | EERPHSHL  | Virtual File hash length              | V U(2)  |
   | 108 | EERPHSH   | Virtual File hash                     | V U(n)  |
   |     | EERPSIGL  | EERP signature length                 | V U(2)  |
   |     | EERPSIG   | EERP signature                        | V U(n)  |
   o-------------------------------------------------------------------o

   EERPCMD   Command Code                                      Character

      Value: 'E'  EERP Command identifier.

   EERPDSN   Virtual File Dataset Name                        String(26)

             Dataset name of the Virtual File being transferred,
             assigned by bilateral agreement.

             No general structure is defined for this attribute.

             See Virtual Files - Identification (Section 1.5.2)

   EERPRSV1  Reserved                                          String(3)

             This field is reserved for future use.

   EERPDATE  Virtual File Date stamp                          Numeric(8)

     Format: 'CCYYMMDD'  8 decimal digits representing the century,
             year, month, and day, respectively.

             Date stamp assigned by the Virtual File's Originator
             indicating when the file was made available for
             transmission.

             See Virtual Files - Identification (Section 1.5.2)

   EERPTIME  Virtual File Time stamp                         Numeric(10)

     Format: 'HHMMSScccc'  10 decimal digits representing hours,
             minutes, seconds, and a counter (0001-9999), which gives
             higher resolution.

             Time stamp assigned by the Virtual File's Originator
             indicating when the file was made available for
             transmission.

             See Virtual Files - Identification (Section 1.5.2)

   EERPUSER  User Data                                         String(8)

             May be used by ODETTE-FTP in any way.  If unused, it should
             be initialised to spaces.  It is expected that a bilateral
             agreement exists as to the meaning of the data.

   EERPDEST  Destination                                      String(25)

     Format: See Identification Code (Section 5.4)

             Originator of the Virtual File.

             This is the location that created the data for
             transmission.

   EERPORIG  Originator                                       String(25)

     Format: See Identification Code (Section 5.4)

             Final Recipient of the Virtual File.

             This is the location that will look into the Virtual File
             content and process it accordingly.  It is also the
             location that creates the EERP for the received file.

   EERPHSHL  Virtual File hash length                          Binary(2)

             Length in octets of the field EERPHSH.

             A binary value of 0 indicates that no hash is present.
             This is always the case if the EERP is not signed.

   EERPHSH   Virtual File hash                                 Binary(n)

             Hash of the transmitted Virtual File, i.e., not the hash of
             the original file.

             The algorithm used is determined by the bilaterally agreed
             cipher suite specified in the SFIDCIPH.

             It is an application implementation issue to validate the
             EERPHSH to ensure that the EERP is acknowledging the exact
             same file as was originally transmitted.

   EERPSIGL  EERP signature length                             Binary(2)

             0 indicates that this EERP has not been signed.

             Any other value indicates the length of EERPSIG in octets
             and indicates that this EERP has been signed.

   EERPSIG   EERP signature                                    Binary(n)

             Contains the [CMS] enveloped signature of the EERP.

             Signature = Sign{EERPDSN
                              EERPDATE
                              EERPTIME
                              EERPDEST
                              EERPORIG
                              EERPHSH}

             Each field is taken in its entirety, including any padding.
             The envelope must contain the original data, not just the
             signature.

             The [CMS] content type used is SignedData.

             The encapsulated content type used is id-data.

             It is an application issue to validate the signature with
             the contents of the EERP.

<<PENDING:UNEDIFACT_EXTRACTS>>
UN/EDIFACT extracts to be added from UNECE before release: syntax service
directory entries for segments UNB and UNZ, the CONTRL message segment UCI and
composite S011, and the code lists for data elements 0083 and 0085.
```

## What to return

Diagnose the single root cause of this ticket. Reply in any form you like,
but end your reply with exactly one fenced ```json block holding an object
with these four keys. Only the last ```json block in your reply is graded.
Give one value per key: a key that holds several options, or a list of
alternatives, scores zero for that key.

cause: exactly one of
  authentication_failure: The OFTP2 session could not be established because a password, identification code or secure authentication check failed.
  character_set_violation: The interchange contains characters outside the agreed syntax identifier's character repertoire.
  compression_not_agreed: A file was sent compressed (or uncompressed) contrary to what the receiver accepts.
  duplicate_interchange: An interchange was rejected because its interchange control reference was already received from this sender.
  duplicate_virtual_file: A virtual file was refused because the receiver already holds a virtual file with the same identification.
  end_to_end_response_not_returned: The file was delivered but the final recipient never returned the end-to-end response.
  file_too_large: The file exceeds a size limit of the receiver.
  interchange_control_count_mismatch: The interchange control count in the trailer does not match the number of messages in the interchange.
  interchange_control_reference_mismatch: The interchange control reference in the header and the trailer differ.
  invalid_destination: The OFTP2 destination of the virtual file is not known to the receiver.
  no_sender_side_fault: Nothing the sender transmitted is wrong; the fault lies with the receiver.
  recipient_identification_mismatch: The interchange recipient identification or its qualifier is not the one in the partner agreement.
  restart_position_invalid: A restarted transfer asked to resume from a position the receiver cannot honour.
  sender_identification_mismatch: The interchange sender identification or its qualifier is not the one in the partner agreement.
  session_parameters_not_negotiated: The sender used an OFTP2 session parameter (credit, buffer size or similar) outside what was negotiated.
  syntax_identifier_not_agreed: The interchange uses a syntax identifier or syntax version other than the agreed one.
  test_indicator_mismatch: The interchange is flagged as test (or production) contrary to the agreement.

layer: exactly one of
  transport: The OFTP2 session or file transfer.
  envelope: The EDIFACT interchange envelope (UNB to UNZ) as checked by the receiver's translator.
  none: There is no fault on the sender side.

owner: exactly one of (who must act to fix the root cause)
  sender: The party that sent the file and raised the ticket must fix it.
  receiver: The trading partner that received the file must fix it.
  agreement: The partner agreement itself is wrong or inconsistent and must be amended before either side can fix the fault.

location: a JSON array of strings.
List every OFTP2 field or EDIFACT data element involved in the fault (the
fields whose values, together, cause the problem) and no others.
Write each one as:
  OFTP2 field:                 COMMAND.FIELD, e.g. "SSID.SSIDCODE"
  EDIFACT simple data element: SEGMENT.ELEMENT, e.g. "UNH.0062"
  EDIFACT component element:   SEGMENT.COMPOSITE.COMPONENT, e.g. "UNB.S004.0017"
  No fault on the sender side: "NONE" on its own.

Example of the format only (not a hint):
```json
{"cause": "file_too_large", "layer": "transport", "owner": "receiver", "location": ["SFID.SFIDFSIZ"]}
```

response_text:
## Diagnosis

The fault is an interchange control reference mismatch on the sender side. The transport worked, and the translator rejected the envelope.

- **UNB** carries interchange control reference `174080`: `UNB+UNOA:3+LARKSPAN73:ZZ+CORRANDALE92:ZZ+261030:0713+174080'`
- **UNZ** closes with `174800`: `UNZ+1+174800'`

The two references differ by a transposition of the last two digits. The UNZ count of 1 is correct, so the count is not the problem.

The receiver's CONTRL confirms this. It echoes the UNB reference `174080` in UCI and gives reason 0085, REFERENCES_DO_NOT_MATCH.

The rest of the transmission is consistent:

- The OFTP2 session parameters match the agreement: SSIDLEV 5, SSIDSDEB 4096, SSIDCRED 64, no compression, no file security.
- The virtual file's SFIDDSN, SFIDORIG, SFIDDEST, SFIDDATE and SFIDTIME match the agreement and the UNB date and time.
- The sender and recipient identifications and the syntax identifier match the agreement.
- The EERP was matched to the virtual file, so the file was delivered.

The EERP only confirms delivery, not translator acceptance. The customer is right that the file was received, but the interchange itself was invalid on the sender's side. The sender must correct the trailer or header and resend. The customer should not be asked to change anything.

```json
{"cause": "interchange_control_reference_mismatch", "layer": "envelope", "owner": "sender", "location": ["UNB.0020", "UNZ.0020"]}
```
